definition.en: GDP is the total gross value added by resident producers plus taxes and minus product subsidies. Values are in current US dollars.
definition.pt-BR: PIB é o valor adicionado dos produtores residentes, acrescido de impostos e descontados subsídios sobre produtos, em dólares correntes.

limitations.en: Nominal US$ values reflect prices and exchange rates; this is not inflation-adjusted growth. GDP is not household income.
limitations.pt-BR: Valores nominais em US$ refletem preços e câmbio; não representam crescimento real. PIB não é renda domiciliar.

provenance.sourceNote: Gross domestic product is the total income earned through the production of goods and services in an economic territory during an accounting period. It can be measured in three different ways: using either the expenditure approach, the income approach, or the production approach. This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This indicator is expressed in United States dollars.

definition.en: GDP per capita is GDP divided by midyear population, expressed in current US dollars.
definition.pt-BR: PIB per capita é o PIB dividido pela população no meio do ano, em dólares correntes.

limitations.en: An average, not median income. Not purchasing-power adjusted and not a measure of income distribution.
limitations.pt-BR: É uma média, não a renda mediana. Não é ajustado por poder de compra e não mede distribuição de renda.

provenance.sourceNote: Gross domestic product is the total income earned through the production of goods and services in an economic territory during an accounting period. It can be measured in three different ways: using either the expenditure approach, the income approach, or the production approach. The core indicator has been divided by the general population to achieve a per capita estimate.This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This indicator is expressed in United States dollars.

provenance.attribution: World Bank WDI (VC.IHR.PSRC.P5); original providers: UNODC Research - Data Portal – Intentional Homicide, UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC). WWMaps conversion: divide by 1; no imputation.

definition.en: Victims of unlawful deaths purposefully inflicted by another person, per 100,000 people. WDI distributes UNODC intentional-homicide data.
definition.pt-BR: Vítimas de mortes ilícitas intencionalmente causadas por outra pessoa, por 100 mil habitantes. O WDI distribui dados de homicídios intencionais da UNODC.

limitations.en: Registration coverage, criminal-justice systems and definitions differ. Counts, war deaths and other violent deaths are not interchangeable with this rate.
limitations.pt-BR: Cobertura de registro, sistemas de justiça e definições variam. Contagens, mortes em guerra e outras mortes violentas não equivalem a essa taxa.

provenance.sourceNote: An intentional homicide is defined as an unlawful death inflicted upon a person with the intent to cause death or serious injury.
provenance.sourceOrganization: UNODC Research - Data Portal – Intentional Homicide, UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC)

definition.en: Number of live births during the year per 1,000 people, using the estimated midyear population.
definition.pt-BR: Nascidos vivos durante o ano por mil habitantes, usando a população estimada no meio do ano.

limitations.en: Crude birth rate depends on population age structure. It is not the fertility rate (children per woman). Series may include demographic estimates.
limitations.pt-BR: A taxa bruta depende da estrutura etária. Não é a taxa de fecundidade (filhos por mulher). A série pode incluir estimativas demográficas.

provenance.sourceNote: Crude birth rate indicates the number of live births occurring during the year, per 1,000 population estimated at midyear. Subtracting the crude death rate from the crude birth rate provides the rate of natural increase, which is equal to the rate of population change in the absence of migration.

provenance.originalUnit: Percent of population below US$3.00/day (2021 PPP)
provenance.attribution: World Bank WDI (SI.POV.DDAY); original providers: World Bank, Poverty and Inequality Platform. Data are based on primary household survey data obtained from government statistical agencies and World Bank country departments. Data for high-income economies are mostly from the Luxembourg Income Study database. For more information and methodology, please see http://pip.worldbank.org., World Bank (WB), uri: http://pip.worldbank.org, note: Data are based on primary household survey data obtained from government statistical agencies and World Bank country departments. Data for high-income economies are mostly from the Luxembourg Income Study database.. WWMaps conversion: divide by 1; no imputation.

definition.en: Share of the population living below US$3.00 per person per day at 2021 purchasing-power parity.
definition.pt-BR: Parcela da população abaixo de US$3,00 por pessoa por dia, em paridade de poder de compra de 2021.

limitations.en: Do not mix with older US$2.15/2017 PPP or US$1.90/2011 PPP vintages. Household-survey availability varies; an absent year is not zero poverty.
limitations.pt-BR: Não misture com revisões antigas de US$2,15/PPC 2017 ou US$1,90/PPC 2011. Pesquisas domiciliares têm disponibilidade variável; ano ausente não significa pobreza zero.

provenance.sourceNote: Poverty headcount ratio at $3.00 a day is the percentage of the population living on less than $3.00 a day at 2021 purchasing power adjusted prices. As a result of revisions in PPP exchange rates, poverty rates for individual countries cannot be compared with poverty rates reported in earlier editions.
provenance.sourceOrganization: World Bank, Poverty and Inequality Platform. Data are based on primary household survey data obtained from government statistical agencies and World Bank country departments. Data for high-income economies are mostly from the Luxembourg Income Study database. For more information and methodology, please see http://pip.worldbank.org., World Bank (WB), uri: http://pip.worldbank.org, note: Data are based on primary household survey data obtained from government statistical agencies and World Bank country departments. Data for high-income economies are mostly from the Luxembourg Income Study database.

definition.en: Years a newborn would live if prevailing age-specific mortality rates stayed constant throughout life.
definition.pt-BR: Anos que um recém-nascido viveria se as taxas de mortalidade por idade observadas permanecessem constantes ao longo da vida.

limitations.en: A period life-table indicator, not a prediction of the actual lifespan of this birth cohort. Series may use modeled estimates.
limitations.pt-BR: Indicador de tábua de vida de período, não uma previsão da longevidade real dessa coorte. Séries podem usar estimativas modeladas.

provenance.sourceNote: Life expectancy at birth indicates the number of years a newborn infant would live if prevailing patterns of mortality at the time of its birth were to stay the same throughout its life.
